data:
This course will aim to introduce the students to the basic concepts of Macroeconomics. Transitioning from the individual and firm behaviour of microeconomics, it will focus on the aggregate economy incomes and economic growth.  It will build on the introductory concepts like consumption, savings, investment, government spending, GDP, money, inflation, wages, unemployment, current and capital accounts, fiscal deficits, role of expectations etc. Students will learn about the engine room of the macroeconomic world- the aggregate demand function and the IS and LM.
Topics: Economic methods, Defining and measuring macroeconomic aggregates-national output and income-CPI, WPI, Deflator, Introduction to Aggregate Incomes-Growth, Productivity, & Technology, Unemployment, Inflation, Core of Macroeconomics-Aggregate Expenditure and Equilibrium Output, Government- Fiscal Policy, Credit Markets and the Monetary System. Aggregate Demand and Aggregate Supply. Introduction to ISLM Framework.
Introduction to Finance: Concepts and Methods
